deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

description.description: One or more paragraphs of text description of a CertificateIssuanceConfig.

key_algorithm.description: Key algorithm to use when generating the private key. Possible values: ["RSA_2048", "ECDSA_P256"]
key_algorithm.rationale: The key algorithm affects the cryptographic strength and type of private key generated for issued certificates.

labels.description:
'Set of label tags associated with the CertificateIssuanceConfig resource.
 An object containing a list of "key": value pairs. Example: { "name": "wrench", "count": "3" }.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.

lifetime.description:
Lifetime of issued certificates. A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, ending with 's'.
Example: "1814400s". Valid values are from 21 days (1814400s) to 30 days (2592000s)
lifetime.rationale: Certificate lifetime affects how long an issued certificate remains valid. A shorter approved lifetime reduces the exposure window if a certificate is misused.

location.description: The Certificate Manager location. If not specified, "global" is used.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.description:
A user-defined name of the certificate issuance config.
CertificateIssuanceConfig names must be unique globally.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

rotation_window_percentage.description:
It specifies the percentage of elapsed time of the certificate lifetime to wait before renewing the certificate.
Must be a number between 1-99, inclusive.
You must set the rotation window percentage in relation to the certificate lifetime so that certificate renewal occurs at least 7 days after
the certificate has been issued and at least 7 days before it expires.
rotation_window_percentage.rationale: The rotation window controls when renewal starts. An approved rotation window helps renewal occur before expiry and supports predictable certificate lifecycle management.

certificate_authority_config.description: The CA that issues the workload certificate. It includes the CA address, type, authentication to CA service, etc.

certificate_authority_config.certificate.description:
A CA pool resource used to issue a certificate.
The CA pool string has a relative resource path following the form
"projects/{project}/locations/{location}/caPools/{caPool}".
certificate_authority_config.certificate.rationale: A relative resource path (projects/*/locations/*/caPools/*) pointing at the CA pool that issues the certificate. This is a reference to another resource; platform policy does not constrain which CA pool a team points at any more than it constrains other resource references, and enforcing a specific pool would require hardcoding a project/name we cannot know.
